clue.text: 50% clemency I soon arranged that can cut sentence

indicators.note: letters that are arranged are put into a new order, so the pool is shuffled
half of a word: the first four of the eight letters of clemency

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone shows only half the mercy they might, and arranges a reduced punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: '50%' takes CLEM, the first half of 'clemency'; 'arranged' shuffles CLEM + I + SOON. 'Sentence' is the grammatical kind, not a prison term.
explanation.definitionFit: This punctuation mark divides a written sentence into parts, so it cuts it.

clue.text: Plant rescued from refuse dump

indicators.note: something rescued from a place is pulled out of it, so the letters are taken from within the words

explanation.surface: A gardener salvages a plant someone threw on the tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rescued from' takes the run SEDUM out of 'refuSE DUMp'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedum is a genus of succulent plants, often called stonecrop.

clue.text: Moving piece includes a song in Oriental language

indicators.note: one piece including another holds it inside

parts.note: a man is a piece moved in chess or draughts
taken as written
a lay is an old word for a song or ballad

explanation.surface: A touching piece of music contains a song in an Eastern tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' suggests emotional, but here it describes a piece moved on a board, as in draughts.
explanation.definitionFit: The tongue of Malaya, known as Malay, is an Eastern language.

clue.text: Lots of puzzles man copied illegitimately

indicators.note: done illegitimately, irregularly, so the letters are not in their proper order

explanation.surface: A man has plagiarised a large number of puzzles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'illegitimately' rearranges the letters of MAN COPIED.
explanation.definitionFit: Compendiums are collections, such as volumes gathering many puzzles together.

clue.text: March issue of book

parts.note: looks like a magazine's March edition; really the offspring of the March family in a famous novel, which is also the title

explanation.surface: A magazine's March edition.
explanation.walkthrough: Issue means offspring: the four March daughters of Louisa May Alcott's novel, whose title names them.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcott's novel is about the March girls, the children of the family.

clue.text: Put up head of family to sign agreement

indicators.note: in a down entry, put up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: a don is the head of a Mafia family

explanation.surface: A family head is installed to sign a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up' turns DON upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A nod of the head is a gesture signalling assent.

clue.text: Fraction that's taken by Americans in self-defence

definitions.text: that's taken by Americans in self-defence
definitions.meaning: Americans plead the ... Amendment to avoid incriminating themselves

explanation.walkthrough: To 'take the Fifth' is to refuse to answer under the US Constitution's Fifth Amendment.
explanation.definitionFit: One of five equal parts is a simple fraction.

clue.text: Reason for temperature being given in Fahrenheit always

parts.note: ever means always, as in ever hopeful

explanation.surface: Explaining a high reading by giving it in Fahrenheit every time.
explanation.definitionFit: Illness with a raised body heat is what causes a patient to run a temperature.

clue.text: Entertainment that's not just associated with female

parts.note: unjust is unfair

explanation.surface: An entertainment linked with women is unjust to men.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairground with rides and stalls is a form of entertainment.

clue.text: Thrash organiser of party after heroin's found

indicators.note: the party organiser comes after the drug in the answer

parts.note: horse is slang for heroin
a whip enforces discipline among a political party's members

explanation.surface: A party organiser is beaten after being found with drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat someone with a riding lash is to thrash them.

clue.text: Mark boundary between food store and college

parts.note: a deli, short for delicatessen, sells food
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: Drawing a line between the deli and the campus.
explanation.definitionFit: To fix the limits of something is to mark its boundary.

clue.text: Person eating about six, one conjectures

indicators.note: one piece eating another takes it inside

parts.note: a diner is someone eating

indicators.note: about signals turning round, so the Roman six is read backwards

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone at dinner for about six guesses something.
explanation.walkthrough: Roman six is turned round by 'about', and 'eating' puts the result inside the person eating.
explanation.definitionFit: A soothsayer or guesser divines, making conjectures about the unknown.

clue.text: Live on a month, perhaps

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after

parts.note: May is a month
to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: Getting by on one month's money.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words express possibility, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Letter-box? I won't go into that

definitions.text: Letter-box? I won't go into that

parts.words: Letter-box? I won't go into that
parts.note: a typesetter's box of small letters, into which the capital form of the pronoun I does not fit

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to discuss a letter-box.
explanation.walkthrough: Type was stored in cases; the small letters were kept in the bottom one. The pronoun I is always a capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Small letters are named after the printer's bottom type case.

clue.text: Art we perversely distort as type of painting

indicators.note: perversely means contrarily, so the letters go in a wrong order

parts.note: to colour a story is to distort it

explanation.surface: Art we have twisted is a form of painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perversely' turns ART WE into WATER.
explanation.definitionFit: Paintings with pigments mixed in water are a common type.

clue.text: Jail-bird

definitions.meaning: a slang term for a prison, short for penitentiary

explanation.definitionFit: Penitentiary shortens to a word for prison, and the same word names a female swan.

clue.text: Revolting animals were so stubborn

definitions.meaning: in Orwell's Animal Farm, the animals in revolt were led by pigs

explanation.walkthrough: Read the first part as 'pig-headed', led by pigs, as in Animal Farm.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstinate people are said to be as headstrong as a pig.

clue.text: Have the landed gentry become so unpretentious?

definitions.text: Have the landed gentry become so
definitions.meaning: people who have landed have come down to the ground

explanation.walkthrough: 'Landed gentry' means owners of estates; read 'landed' as having touched ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone practical and modest is described with this idiom.

clue.text: Surprising, revelation as lids are raised

definitions.meaning: a surprising revelation is an unexpected discovery
eyelids lift to open the eyes

explanation.walkthrough: 'lids' are eyelids, not saucepan lids.
explanation.definitionFit: A startling discovery is idiomatically something that makes you open your eyes wide.

clue.text: Grenadier ordered to include me for foreign force

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take the other piece inside
put in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grenadier is commanded to take me into a foreign army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks military beside 'Grenadier' but is the anagram signal; 'to include' puts the second piece inside the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A French corps of armed police is a force from abroad.

clue.text: People least affected by the gravity of their situation

definitions.text: People least affected by the gravity of their situation

parts.words: People least affected by the gravity of their situation
parts.note: seems to mean people unfazed by a serious plight; really people who live so high in the Himalayas that gravity is weakest

explanation.surface: Folk who stay calm in a serious crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: Natives of a Himalayan country live at the highest altitudes, where gravity pulls least.

clue.text: Fruit with it

explanation.definitionFit: A rose's fruit bears this name, and the same word is slang for fashionable.

clue.text: Agreement to provide mostly hard cash, except for one note

indicators.note: most of a word, so its final letter goes

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: except for signals leaving out a letter

parts.note: money is cash
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A deal to supply mostly hard cash, apart from one bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts HARD to HAR; 'except for' removes E from MONEY to leave MONY. 'Note' looks like a banknote but is musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Accord between people is harmony, a synonym of agreement.

clue.text: Unnaturally neat prose?

indicators.note: unnaturally means artificially, so the letters are made into an artificial arrangement

explanation.surface: Writing that is suspiciously tidy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unnaturally' rearranges NEAT PROSE; the whole clue also defines it, as this is an artificial, invented language.
explanation.definitionFit: Zamenhof's constructed language is an artificial tongue with regular grammar.

clue.text: Prepare money for immediate use

definitions.meaning: to ... something is to prepare it

explanation.walkthrough: 'The ready' is British slang for available cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Make ready means prepare, and the word is also slang for cash on hand.

clue.text: City man whose break-up of partnership led to long-term investment

definitions.text: man whose break-up of partnership led to long-term investment
definitions.meaning: the Trojan prince who took Helen from her husband, causing the ten-year siege of Troy

explanation.walkthrough: 'Investment' is the old military sense: besieging a city. The surface suggests finance.
explanation.definitionFit: The French capital shares its name with the Trojan prince who eloped with Helen.

clue.text: Likewise, hat is cone-shaped, say

parts.note: so means likewise, as in 'so do I'
lid is slang for a hat

explanation.surface: Similarly, this hat comes to a point.
explanation.definitionFit: A cone is an example of a three-dimensional geometric figure.

clue.text: In strange dialect, big-mouthed?

indicators.note: strange suggests something odd, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: In an odd accent, someone is a loudmouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges DIALECT. 'Big-mouthed' looks like boastful; it means having a delta, a wide river mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A river delta is a broad, branching mouth, so this adjective fits a river with a big mouth.

clue.text: Put cover on small explosive device

definitions.meaning: a tiny charge for a toy gun

explanation.definitionFit: To top something is to cover it, and the same word names a toy gun's small percussion charge.

clue.text: Have objective that aids the opposition

parts.note: to own is to have
a goal is an objective

explanation.surface: Pursuing an aim that helps your rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting the ball in your own net gives the opposing team a point.

clue.text: Fair old coin I toss

parts.note: D was the abbreviation for the old British penny
taken as written
to shy is to throw or toss

explanation.surface: Someone flips an ancient coin to decide fairly.
explanation.walkthrough: D stood for a penny before British decimal currency in 1971. 'Fair' means good-looking, not just.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair in the old sense of attractive, and dishy is slang for good-looking.

clue.text: Provided picture for editor with wine and fish

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: Someone supplied an illustration to the editor, along with wine and fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Depicted in art means having supplied a picture of something.
